name: 远瀛观 Yuanyingguan
line: Modelled from plate 14 of 1783-86, Ohlmer's and Piry's photographs of the clock gate (1873, 1876), the ruin photographs since 1900, Durand's survey (S603) and the plan S01; every figure is a reading (C) unless the row says otherwise. The rear, the ends and the body behind the centre are carried round (assumed).
rows: 31 × 35 m (S603, survey, B; which way is not stated: Q67), its top 4.3 m above its foot, where 大水法's stairs arrive (Round 15, C, Q232); retaining walls of piers and long rusticated stones (S603, B; the pier spacing assumed); paved; the front balustrade with urns, the side balustrades, eight trees in square pits (plate 14, C); a stair down at the back (assumed, for reach)

28 × 21 m (S603's post grid, B; Q67), an inverted 凹 (S310, B): two wings with chamfered corners come 4.5 m forward of the centre block (plate 14, C); on a base 1.2 m high (P0216, P0757, C); grey brick dressed with white marble (S02 p.155, B); the cornice 8 m above the terrace (P0183, C)

the door (1.9 × 4.2 m) between two carved columns 6 m apart on pedestals, their capitals 7.1 m above the terrace, an entablature block over each standing proud (P0183 of 1873, P0216, P0757, C); a lion on each pedestal (plate 14 only, C); the attic with the clock wheel, its arched moulding and crest 11.7 m above the terrace (P0183, plate 14: they agree, C); a door-like opening either side (P0179, P0216, C)

a big window on a carved sill block in each wing's front, pilasters on every face and chamfer; a low roof of eight slopes, a deck with a balustrade and a square lantern with a clock face on every side, its finial 14.2 m above the terrace (plate 14; S603 p.133, C)

over the centre: a fish-scale hipped roof as wide as the block, the main hipped roof to 13.2 m pierced by the attic, a pedestal band and the crown at 15.5 m (plate 14; S603 p.133, C); the body behind under a hipped Chinese roof (S603, B; its form assumed); glazed green tile (the 2016 dig found glazed fittings, S153; the colour assumed, Q69)

the front's module is the columns' spacing, 6 m: plate 14's ratios against Durand's 28 m and P0216's door (C); the dossier's 4.2 m made the whole front 18 m. Heights from the photographs where they show the part (the order), from plate 14 scaled by the attic where they agree (the roofs)
the hall's rear and end faces, the body behind, the terrace's south face behind 大水法 and the back stair: carried round from the front (C, the pale tint with conf=1)
